analysis: Q2 reveals different backbones leading to a D classification decided at Q3. Both proofs construct the icosahedron, inscribe it in the given sphere, and prove its side is minor, sharing the core mathematical facts (XIII.10 for equilateral triangles, XIII.9 for the golden ratio property, XIII.11 for the minor classification). However, the intermediate paths diverge substantively. Heath constructs the elevated pentagon QRSTU by proving perpendiculars to the same plane are parallel (XI.6) and using I.33 to establish equal-and-parallel sides, then verifies the circumsphere using XIII.3 (the lesser-segment-squared plus half-greater-segment-squared relation). The AI instead constructs two parallel pentagons rotated by 36 degrees directly, uses coordinate-style distance calculations with I.47 (Pythagorean theorem) and algebraic manipulation of XIII.9 for the circumsphere verification, bypassing both XI.6/I.33 and XIII.3 entirely. These are genuine backbone differences: the heath_only items 1.33, 11.6, and 13.3 represent substantive intermediate steps not present in the AI proof, while the AI's use of 1.47, coordinate geometry, and direct algebraic deduction from 13.9 constitutes a different but valid logical chain. The AI proof is logically complete under the hardened Q1(b) standard, so Q3 yields D.
